title: Runtime daybook — short notes and triage
content:
Quick log for the day — scratchpad style. Short, messy, actionable.

Context:
- Working on intermittent OOMs on raptor-prod when sequence len bursts to ~8k tokens. Not constant; correlates with a small subset of requests that do very long single-turn generations (~7.5–8k).
- Hypothesis 1: memory fragmentation + pinned CUDA allocations causing allocation failures on the largest batches.
- Hypothesis 2: KV-cache page eviction path doesn't free quickly enough under head-of-line blocking; hot requests hold onto >1.5GB each.

Top priorities (today):
- [ ] Reproduce a clean failure in a perf env with debug allocator flags (CUDA_API_LOG or MALLOC_TRACE)
- [ ] Add tracepoint in kv_cache.cpp to mark evict start/end + size freed
- [ ] Try force-compact heuristic (free smaller blocks preemptively) in local build, measure tail latency impact
- [ ] Draft runbook steps for oncall (short-term mitigation = lower max-seq for bursty routes)

Commands / quick repro notes:
- Local repro (approx): ./serve --model raptor-13b --seq-max 8192 --batch-max 8 --kv-cache-mode=dynamic --log-level=debug
- Perf capture: sudo env CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 nvprof --profile-from-start off --log-file nvprof-$(date +%s).log ./serve ...
- Heap snapshot: run with MALLOC_CONF=prof:true,lg_prof_sample:16 to get jemalloc profiles (works in dev image)

Observations from a short run (2 small attempts):
- At t+38s, allocation failed at cudaMalloc 1.2GB when two long requests co-occurred.
- Before fail, RSS on host was ~27GB (instance has 64GB host + 48GB GPU).
- Worker process had many small free blocks; fragmentation visible in jemalloc output.

Immediate experiments to try (order):
1) Rebuild with jemalloc purge hooks: call nn_runtime::purge_unused_memory() after large-generation flush — see if host RSS drops and prevents OOMs. Measure 50 runs.
2) Force KV-cache eager eviction when pending queue length > 2 — simple guardrail to reduce peak per-request memory. 3 runs per config.
3) Switch allocator to managed pool (pre-reserve 24GB on startup) to avoid dynamic cudaMalloc churn. Worst-case increases steady memory but might reduce bursts.

Measurements to record:
- peak GPU mem (nvidia-smi sample every 1s), host RSS, per-request max_kv_bytes, latency p50/p95/p99.
- record which model shard/placement used (we saw one case on shard B causing localized high usage).

Notes to include in runbook (short):
- If OOM observed on prod route x: set env ROUTE_MAX_SEQ=4096 for 30m for that route and contact runtime-oncall.
- If top-of-queue backlog > 50 and avg latency > 2x baseline, trigger fallback to raptor-8b variant.

Bugs & short tickets to open:
- RINF-1973: kv-evict race when concurrent evict/append — include repro steps and sample jemalloc profile. (Assigned to Ravi)
- RINF-1981: long seq allocations not respecting pooling hints — follow up with release-eng for allocator knob.

Design note (brain-dump) — per-request token budget window:
- Idea: introduce a soft cap per request for kv-cache bytes at generation time (e.g., soft_kv_limit = min(max_kv, total_tokens_so_far * k)) so we can degrade gracefully rather than OOM. Needs: model-aware k, safety for function-calls/long-context special cases.
- Implementation: check at each kv append; if append pushes request over soft_kv_limit, signal cooperative truncation of prefill (drop oldest prefixes) or switch to streaming fallback.

Hand-off / tomorrow:
- Pair with Jules on the jemalloc purge PoC (15–30m pairing).
- Post a short note in #runtime-ops with initial repro and attach nvprof logs.
- If Purge PoC reduces host RSS by >15% on 50 runs, prepare a canary patch for staging and small canary in prod (route with low traffic).

Misc notes / ideas for later:
- Investigate a shim layer that slices very long single-turn requests into chunked prefill writes to reduce per-request kv peaks (adds latency but reduces memory spikes).
- Explore a lightweight scheduler that limits concurrent long-gen requests across a pool (cooperative admission controller).

End of day quick status:
- Repro: partial, see allocation at t+38s in dev. Need more stable repro.
- Next step: jemalloc purge hook PoC + add kv tracepoints.

Micro-tasks (two-minute wins):
- [ ] Add link to RINF-1973 in this doc and paste initial jemalloc profile file path once uploaded.
- [ ] Send quick Slack ping to runtime-oncall channel with repro outline.

Timeboxing:
- Morning (9:00–11:00): repro + jemalloc profiling
- Midday (11:30–13:00): pair PoC with Jules
- Afternoon (14:00–17:00): implement kv tracepoints + test forced-evict heuristic

Personal: take 10–15m walk after lunch to clear head before digging into allocator internals.

-- Imani
